solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Out of order lift wanted — she's being thick

indicators.note: something out of order is jumbled up, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken lift has made someone cross, and she's being obtuse about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' reads as a description of the lift but signals rearranging LIFT WANTED SHE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupidity, the state of being dim or dense, is the meaning of the long noun.

clue.text: Top Gear presenter — one that can't take over writing

indicators.note: the first piece sits over the second, covering it, so the second goes inside

parts.note: a hater is someone who cannot take, or stand, something
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A TV motoring presenter is painted as someone unable to cope with writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Hammond, presenter of the BBC motoring show Top Gear, was nicknamed 'the Hamster'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname of Richard Hammond, one of the long-running presenters of the British car programme.

clue.text: Somewhere a film stunt is shot for sitcom

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or ruined, so these letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A location shoot where a film stunt takes place for a TV comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is shot' looks like filming language but tells you to rearrange SOMEWHERE A FILM STUNT. The answer is the long-running BBC comedy set in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a long-running BBC situation comedy about three elderly men in Yorkshire.

clue.text: See 2
Some mints will get you by when you're talking

indicators.note: speech is involved, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: in multiplication, 'by' means times, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A suggestion that some mints will see you through while you chat.
explanation.walkthrough: Thyme belongs to the mint family of plants, Lamiaceae.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a herb of the mint family, so its varieties are examples of mints.

clue.text: Old record company values stadium

parts.note: EMI was a famous British record label, now absorbed into others
rates are values or prices, as in exchange rates

explanation.surface: A former record label puts a price on a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Emirates Stadium is Arsenal football club's home in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal's football ground in London is named after its airline sponsor.

clue.text: Carries on lifting a single pound — very heavy?

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the words upward, so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tote is to carry
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone struggles on lifting a single pound and finds it very heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very heavy' seems to describe a weight but refers to heavy traffic, with cars bumper to bumper.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy traffic is so dense that vehicles queue bumper to bumper, a phrase for congestion.

clue.text: Short hit, most of strength kept in reserve

indicators.note: the inner letters are held within the reserve word

parts.note: a stash is a hidden reserve
rapped means struck or hit

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for strength is dropped

parts.note: force is strength or power

explanation.surface: A short blow, with most of one's strength held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of the hit but is the definition: short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short means lacking money, the colloquial sense of being hard up.

clue.text: Wheel cuts through mushroom

indicators.note: the wheel word cuts into the middle of the other word

parts.note: by means through or via, as in travelling by Paris
to wheel is to roll

explanation.surface: A wheel slices through a fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: An opened umbrella has the domed shape of a mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An opened umbrella looks like a mushroom cap on a stalk, a playful visual likeness.

clue.text: Building where Holy Mother swaddles Jesus?

indicators.note: swaddling wraps a baby, so the mother's name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Mary is the mother of Jesus
Jesus is the Son of God

explanation.surface: A nativity scene: in a building, Mary wraps the infant Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonework or brickwork used in construction; building in the sense of the structure made.

clue.text: Elected American sent over article taken from Rear Admiral?

parts.note: elected candidates are in

indicators.note: sent over means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: US for United States, American

indicators.note: the article is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An elected US official sends over an item seized from a rear admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral is a British car insurance company; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral is a well-known British motor insurance firm, so it is an example of the class.

clue.text: Newcastle's very nice, no formality

parts.note: too means very, as in not too bad

indicators.note: no means without, so the letters for formality are removed

parts.note: taken as written
ice is coldness or formality of manner

explanation.surface: A visitor praises Newcastle as very pleasant and relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Toon is the Geordie name for Newcastle upon Tyne and its football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Local dialect for 'town', used as a nickname for the city and Newcastle United.

clue.text: Crimean port does not let through returning Israeli actor

indicators.note: returning means the goalkeeping word is read backwards

parts.note: a goalkeeper who saves does not let the ball through
Chaim Topol, the Israeli actor famed for Fiddler on the Roof

explanation.surface: A Crimean port's border guards turn back a returning Israeli actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is a Black Sea harbour and naval base on the Crimean peninsula.

clue.text: Clarinet delivered, plus hard parts

indicators.note: the inner letters part the word for delivered, splitting it

parts.note: a baby delivered is born
a plus is an advantage, an asset
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A clarinet is delivered along with some hard components.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an alto member of the clarinet family, as used by Mozart.

clue.text: Light colour on desert palm

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A pale shade set against a desert palm tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' is a verb here, to rat, not sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattan is a climbing palm whose stems are used for cane furniture.

clue.text: Whimsical about Earth, possibly how it feels to touch down

definitions.text: how it feels to touch down

indicators.note: the first word goes about, around, the rest

parts.note: fey means whimsical or otherworldly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be another arrangement

explanation.surface: A whimsical musing on landing back on Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch down' suggests a plane landing, but down here is soft plumage that you touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft plumage is light and fluffy to the touch, like the plumes of a bird.

clue.text: Cut up OK-ish minced Russian delicacies

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: to rip is to cut or tear

indicators.note: minced means chopped finely, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cook chops up some so-so ingredients for minced Russian snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small Russian pastries filled with meat or vegetables, a delicacy of that cuisine.

clue.text: Religious jerk, about 18

indicators.note: the jerk word goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk
the answer at 18 across is a verb for stealing; a heist is a theft

explanation.surface: A religious jerk is described as roughly the number eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Believing in God or gods is the core of religious belief.

clue.text: Future book about military chap

indicators.note: the book word goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: a tome is a large book
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A futuristic book about a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes what lies ahead, as in the years ahead; adjectival sense of future.

clue.text: Turn again, going back to lift

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to reflip is to turn over again

explanation.surface: Turning again and going back to a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift is slang for to steal, especially small items.

clue.text: Black and blue after game — what's needed?

indicators.note: the bruise pieces come after the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
blue and down both mean sad

explanation.surface: Someone black and blue after a match asks what treatment is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A massage is what a bruised player needs after a rugby match.

clue.text: Foundation provider when I go short

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a go is a move, a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone who lays foundations says when they leave it is too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: Foundation is Isaac Asimov's science-fiction series.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov wrote the Foundation novels, so as their author he provided them.

clue.text: Its procedure may imprison you?

parts.note: a court building's proceedings may end in a jail sentence for you

explanation.walkthrough: The trials held in a judicial building can end with a jail sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A building housing courts of law, whose trials may lead to imprisonment.

clue.text: About to wind up pirate

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for circa, about
to rib is to tease or wind up

explanation.surface: Someone is about to provoke a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pirate' is a verb: to copy or plagiarise.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy another's work without permission is the verb sense of both words.

clue.text: Wife's endless cheating

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: fraud is cheating or deception

explanation.surface: A wife caught in endless infidelity.
explanation.definitionFit: German title for a married woman, used in English for a German wife.

clue.text: Huge old lady — gypsy?

parts.note: mam is a colloquial word for mother, one's old lady
the gypsy moth is a species of moth

explanation.surface: A large elderly woman is asked if she is a Romany.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous, after the extinct giant woolly elephant.

clue.text: With strong accent, hurt censor

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or hurt
Cato the Elder was a famous Roman censor

explanation.surface: A writer with a strong accent is wounded by a censor.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical direction meaning each note is emphasised or stressed.

clue.text: Singer fled capital, a horrible(!) fan being around

indicators.note: the fan word goes around everything else

parts.note: taken as written
ran means fled
Kiev is the capital of Ukraine
ugh is an exclamation of disgust at something horrible

explanation.surface: A singer flees a capital city, pursued by a horrible fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The British pop singer Frankie Vaughan was famous for 'Give Me the Moonlight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankie Vaughan was a popular British crooner of the 1950s and 60s.
